init.title: Health contract maintenance
init.description: Select the resource whose health contract you want to review, or reset to the Hubinet Ops built-in default.

reset_confirm.title: Reset the health contract for {name}
reset_confirm.description:
This currently declares:

{current}

Resetting replaces it with the Hubinet Ops built-in default for a package-managed LXC: a single `guest_operational` probe, which proves only that the exact container is still reachable and can still run a process. It does not prove application health.

Hubinet Ops does not discover Docker or systemd workloads for you — absence of a workload observer is not proof of workload absence — so an advanced Docker/systemd contract stays an explicit choice you make with the `hubinet_ops.set_health_contract` action.

Check the box and select **Submit** to confirm.

data.confirm: I understand — restore the built-in default

plan.title: Hubinet Ops update plan — {name}
plan.approval_instruction: Review every row, then press **Approve reviewed plan** on this resource. Approval is refused if the backend, resource, scan, or material fingerprint changes. This review is forgotten when Home Assistant reloads.

health_probes.heading: Per-probe health evidence
health_probes.observation_note: This is bounded observation evidence from the last completed settling round, not a definitive verdict. The job stays active; press **Re-run health evaluation** to evaluate again.

health.title: Hubinet Ops health contract — {name}
health.unconfigured: No health contract is configured. This is **unconfigured**, not healthy, and a package update cannot start until a contract is declared. This is not the normal state: Hubinet Ops gives every package-managed LXC a built-in `guest_operational` contract, and the next successful inventory discovery restores it automatically. To restore it now, use **Settings → Devices & Services → Hubinet Ops → Configure**, or the **`hubinet_ops.reset_health_contract`** action. To declare an advanced contract instead, use **`hubinet_ops.set_health_contract`** — reachable from this device's **Actions** tab, or from Developer Tools → Actions — naming each required probe kind (`systemd_unit_active`, `docker_container_running`, `docker_container_healthy`, or the targetless `guest_operational` guest-liveness probe) and its target.

health_contract_unconfigured.title: {name}: package update blocked on a missing health contract
health_contract_unconfigured.description:
The reviewed package plan for **{name}** is approved, but no health contract is declared, so **Start approved update** stays disabled.

This should not normally happen: Hubinet Ops gives every package-managed LXC a built-in `guest_operational` health contract, and the next successful inventory discovery restores it for this resource automatically. To restore it now, use **Settings → Devices & Services → Hubinet Ops → Configure**, or the `hubinet_ops.reset_health_contract` action for this device. To declare an advanced Docker/systemd contract instead, use the `hubinet_ops.set_health_contract` action (this device's **Actions** tab, or Developer Tools → Actions).

This issue clears itself automatically once a contract exists for this resource.
